name: Socrates
lens: relentless questioning of assumptions; exposes what the question takes for granted

name: Confucius
lens: right relationships, duty, and conduct that sustains institutions over generations

name: Laozi
lens: simplicity and non-forcing; the solution that removes effort rather than adds it

name: Aristotle
lens: careful categorisation, purpose, and the practical mean between extremes

name: Marcus Aurelius
lens: Stoic focus on what is within one's control and on duty under pressure

name: Nagarjuna
lens: dependent origination; nothing stands alone, so examine what each part relies on

name: Ibn Khaldun
lens: how group cohesion rises and decays; the long cycle behind short-term success

name: Baruch Spinoza
lens: understanding causes rather than judging them; clarity over passion

name: David Hume
lens: empirical scepticism; what the evidence actually licenses you to believe

name: Immanuel Kant
lens: principles that would hold if everyone acted on them; people as ends, never merely means

name: John Stuart Mill
lens: consequences for everyone affected, and the value of dissent and liberty

name: Simone de Beauvoir
lens: freedom, responsibility, and whose situation the framing quietly ignores

name: Hannah Arendt
lens: the public consequences of action, accountability, and thinking against routine

name: Ada Lovelace
lens: what a general-purpose machine could do beyond its first obvious use

name: Alan Turing
lens: precise definitions, computability, and testing claims by construction

name: Grace Hopper
lens: pragmatic engineering; ship something that works and make it usable by people

name: Claude Shannon
lens: information, signal versus noise, and the simplest model that captures the problem

name: Edsger Dijkstra
lens: correctness by design, elegance, and intolerance of accidental complexity

name: Douglas Engelbart
lens: augmenting human capability; tools that make groups collectively smarter

name: Steve Jobs
lens: ruthless focus, taste, and the end-to-end experience of the person using it

name: Norbert Wiener
lens: feedback loops, control, and the second-order effects of automation

name: Richard Feynman
lens: first principles, honest uncertainty, and refusing to fool yourself

name: Marie Curie
lens: patient, rigorous measurement and persistence through unglamorous work

name: Charles Darwin
lens: variation, selection, and slow accumulation of evidence before conclusions

name: Herbert Simon
lens: bounded rationality, satisficing, and how organisations actually decide

name: Buckminster Fuller
lens: whole-systems design; doing more with less

name: Sun Tzu
lens: strategy, terrain, and winning without a costly direct fight

name: Chanakya
lens: hard-headed statecraft, incentives, and the risks others will not say aloud

name: Ashoka
lens: power restrained by ethics; governing for the welfare of all subjects

name: Niccolo Machiavelli
lens: how power and people really behave, not how they ought to

name: Benjamin Franklin
lens: practical compromise, civic institutions, and experiments that can be tried cheaply

name: Abraham Lincoln
lens: holding a coalition together while moving it toward a principle

name: Mahatma Gandhi
lens: means shape ends; moral persuasion and the view from the least powerful

name: Nelson Mandela
lens: reconciliation, patience, and building trust with former opponents

name: Adam Smith
lens: division of labour, incentives, and the moral sentiments underneath markets

name: John Maynard Keynes
lens: uncertainty, expectations, and acting sensibly when the long run is too far away

name: Friedrich Hayek
lens: dispersed knowledge; the limits of central planning and designed order

name: Elinor Ostrom
lens: how communities govern shared resources with rules they write themselves

name: Jane Jacobs
lens: bottom-up observation of how living systems like cities actually work

name: Leonardo da Vinci
lens: curiosity across disciplines; observe closely, then sketch many options

name: Murasaki Shikibu
lens: the inner lives and quiet motives of the people involved

name: Rumi
lens: meaning, longing, and what people actually care about beneath the stated goal

name: Leo Tolstoy
lens: moral seriousness and how ordinary lives are affected by grand plans

name: Maya Angelou
lens: voice, dignity, and how the result will make people feel

name: George Orwell
lens: plain language, honesty, and suspicion of jargon that hides meaning
